title: silicon-ledger facet, version 1
description: Extension fields this corpus attaches to a Claim. OpenClaims permits arbitrary extension via `facets`, requiring only `_producer` and `_schemaURL`. This schema describes what this repository puts there, so a consumer can validate or index it without reading our converter.

_producer.description: Bare repository name, NOT a URN. Convention, pinned across both repositories: _producer is the producing repo's short name, so a reader can tell which instrument wrote a record without resolving anything. The companion instrument is silicon-ledger-bench.

_schemaURL.description: Must resolve. A facet pointing at an unreachable schema is a dangling identifier, which is worse than omitting the facet.

kind.description: Our finer-grained category. Claim.claim_type is constrained by the OpenClaims spec to factual|calculation|inference|recommendation|prediction and cannot carry this distinction, so it lives here. Every record: claim_type=factual, plus the real kind in this field.

entities.description: Chips, APIs, projects or models the claim names.

caveat.description: The scope limit that makes the claim not universally true, e.g. 'M3 affected; M1 and M5 Max reportedly unaffected'. Load-bearing: without it a claim is read as universal.

split.description: Holdout records are sealed at creation and never used to build or tune anything, so the corpus can serve as its own evaluation set. This cannot be applied retroactively: once trained on, contamination is permanent.

legacy_confidence.description: RETIRED. The pre-spine label for how a claim was established. Superseded by the OpenClaims Verification object (verification_result + verification_method + validator), which records who checked it, how, and when — questions this field could not answer. Kept only so old records remain readable.

evidence_status.description: Whether the evidence this record cites can still be verified, checked in this order: (1) does the source still hash to the digest pinned at emission? If not -> 'stale': the target changed under a surviving pointer. (2) does the cited passage still occur in it? If not -> 'unlocatable': the pointer was never right. 'ok' = both pass. The two failure modes are sequential and mutually exclusive, which is why this is one field and not two booleans. A record whose status is not 'ok' claims NO Evidence: absence is declared, never asserted. Mirrors the rule that a span not found verbatim in the registered text is rejected at write time, by non-LLM code.
